headline: 3,431 passengers affected as 10 flights from Dhaka cancelled after Saudi airport attacks
summary: The closure of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh following Houthi attacks has disrupted travel for thousands of Bangladeshi passengers.
details: Successive attacks on Saudi aviation facilities, including King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, have caused widespread flight disruptions.
According to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), 10 flights from Dhaka have been cancelled, affecting 3,431 passengers so far.
The cancellations include three flights each from Saudia and Riyadh Air, and two each from Biman Bangladesh Airlines and US-Bangla Airlines.
Yemen's Houthi group claimed responsibility for the attacks on Riyadh and Dammam airports, as well as Saudi oil facilities.
The Houthis have warned airlines and travellers against using Saudi airports and airspace, except for those in the holy cities of Makkah and Madina.
The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) has advised airlines to avoid specific areas of Saudi airspace due to risks from missile and drone attacks.
Additional disruptions have been included: a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight from Dhaka to Dammam was diverted to Doha, and Himalaya Airlines cancelled flights between Kathmandu and Dammam.
The situation remains uncertain for Bangladeshi migrant workers and pilgrims, as airlines continue to assess the security risks.

The cancellations include three flights each from Saudia and Riyadh Air, and two each from Biman Bangladesh Airlines and US-Bangla Airlines.

Yemen's Houthi group claimed responsibility for the attacks on Riyadh and Dammam airports, as well as Saudi oil facilities.

The Houthis have warned airlines and travellers against using Saudi airports and airspace, except for those in the holy cities of Makkah and Madina.

The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) has advised airlines to avoid specific areas of Saudi airspace due to risks from missile and drone attacks.

Additional disruptions have been included: a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight from Dhaka to Dammam was diverted to Doha, and Himalaya Airlines cancelled flights between Kathmandu and Dammam.

headline: Attack on Jatiya Party Chairman GM Quader's Uttara residence vandalised
summary: A group of 30-40 people hurled bricks and stones at the building, shattering windowpanes, while the Chairman was inside having breakfast.
details: The residence of Jatiya Party Chairman GM Quader in Uttara's Sector 7 was attacked by a group of miscreants on Monday morning.
Around 30 to 40 people, carrying banners and claiming to be the general public, gathered outside the residence around 10:30 am.
Ten minutes later, the group began hurling bricks and stones at the building, shattering windowpanes and scattering glass across the drawing room.
GM Quader stated that he was having breakfast when the attack began, but no one was able to enter the house because the main gate was locked.
Uttara West Police Station chief Mohammad Khalid Mansur confirmed the attack, stating that police arrived at the scene after receiving a report around 11 am.
Police found no one at the scene upon arrival, but have since deployed personnel to ensure the situation remains normal.
